records.subagent_summary: With the incumbent hint only 1/8 rollouts scored 1 and all seven failures hit finish_reason=length at the 16384-token cap (execution 149.198), so non-termination is the dominant failure: each one re-derived "but that speaker could just subtract or divide, so this reading is impossible", restarted the same two-reading enumeration, and either exhausted tokens or boxed an unjustified factor. The revision states explicitly that a private value pinning the partner under one fixed structural choice is not a contradiction, adds the mechanism the failures skipped of applying each announcement to the partner coordinate of surviving scenarios rather than only to the speaker's own value, and imposes a build-once/sweep-once budget rule with an explicit ban on restarting.

All 8 round-10 rollouts scored 1 (2999-6016 tokens), so training is saturated and the loss is transfer plus token waste: every rollout reached the modulus ratio early, but the two longest (6016 and 5918 tokens, 12-14 hedges) burned their middle halves on the completing-the-square bookkeeping the incumbent prescribes and on a self-inflicted crisis from evaluating the center point against the locus and concluding the circle was wrong. The incumbent already forbids the sign-error-prone endpoint shortcut but leaves completing the square as a multi-step manual reduction, so this revision replaces it with the portable general-conic reading (A, B, C, D to center and radius with |A|), which is constant-work, sign-safe on any such locus, and diagnoses the line case by A = 0, and it states plainly that the center is not on the locus so spot-checks never land there.

Training scored 3/8 and all five failures ended at the 16384-token cap rather than on a committed wrong answer; each burned its budget building the rotated big square's far vertices and edge lines (repeatedly deriving side vectors and lines like y=-x+2*sqrt(2)), then testing distances and tangency against them, and one had already reached the right union before losing it in that search. The incumbent asserts a corner covers only a wedge but gives no license to discard the other edges, so the student keeps carrying them. This revision supplies the checkable range condition (the non-adjacent edges lie a full side length from the corner, beyond the farthest point of S, so they cannot cut it) which collapses the cover to two signed linear tests and removes the vertex/tangency computation that consumed every failure.

My 8 public rollouts with the incumbent scored 6/8 and both failures were token-cap truncations, not wrong answers; each had already accepted the N x deg P bound and then stalled on the tightness step. Both looped on the same false obstruction, demanding that a single function's own values across its block themselves step by the progression's difference and concluding the function 'would have to be linear, which it isn't', so they discarded the construction and restarted. The revision keeps the proven bound skeleton verbatim but replaces the vague 'interpolate, free coefficients remain' clause with the explicit portable device P = T + c times the product of (x - n_j) over the block's d indices, which visibly keeps full degree while agreeing with the target exactly there.

7/8 rollouts correct; the single failure did the whole pipeline right and died on one step, evaluating the recovered vertex height by rewriting the small argument as a power of the reciprocal base and copying that exponent, so it got a height of the wrong sign and an area from an off-graph point. All seven correct rollouts instead matched the argument to a power of the base as literally written (one visibly caught itself mid-slip), so the revision adds that inverse-direction read rule plus an argument-magnitude sign check, since the incumbent only covered the forward height-to-argument direction.

My 8 rollouts scored 1/8: five reached 1/8 on part a by counting free binary steps but then abandoned that mechanism for part b, substituting an equally-likely-position shortcut (1/4) or a single lone 1/2, and two instead claimed the outcome is forced. So the incumbent's pricing rule is usable but the students drop it mid-problem and never bound the run they need to control. The revision names the shortest deciding prefix as the object to price, notes that later steps cost nothing, and demands the same procedure be reused on every sub-question.

My 8 rollouts scored 3/8 and all five failures hit the 16384-token cap, never a wrong-formula stop: three carried a botched small case forward (one produced a denominator of 791, one declared n=4 contradictory then looped re-solving it, one re-derived n=4 while already holding a candidate) and two drifted into polynomial-coefficient sign bookkeeping. So the ladder mechanism works but the toy solutions are unverified, and the incumbent only validates the fitted formula, never the individual cases feeding it. This revision inserts a per-case back-substitution check plus an explicit 'a stall means mis-solved toy, recheck arithmetic' rule, and trims 186 tokens to 143 since heldout accuracy across rounds 1-9 fell roughly monotonically with hint length.

6/8 public rollouts were correct; both failures shared one mode and neither was arithmetic: each asserted the stated number of equal groups as the number of units, divided every listed total by it, saw whole quotients, and never invoked gcd or maximality. The incumbent's grouping clause states the multiple constraint only as a prohibition and was ignored; rounds 5-9 all attacked this mode with extra prohibitions or divisibility apparatus at 187-190 tokens and every one collapsed heldout from 0.2125 to 0.0625-0.1375. So I kept the incumbent's spine, ordering and length and made the grouping clause constructive instead of prohibitive, naming the missing second factor via N = groups x units-per-group, and spent the budget by dropping the commute clause that no correct rollout used.

All 8 public rollouts were correct (8/8, 3.5k-8.6k tokens, none truncated), so the training question stays saturated and every remaining point is transfer. Two residual wastes are visible: the 8.6k outlier (roughly double the median) raised the inner coefficient as well as the offset when composing the centered maps, producing a lopsided relation whose spurious extra powers it then solved by guessing four integer centers before recovering; and six of eight rollouts, having verified the solution by roughly their midpoint, spent the tail hunting for 'another fixed point' or doubting that the centered form was a legitimate assumption. This revision keeps the proven trigger, centered ansatz, factored both-branch condition, parameter-count closure and symmetric-combination steps and adds only that the center is an unknown to solve for and that composition multiplies coefficients while raising the offset, so the exponent slip and the second-center hunt both lose their cause.

3/8 correct with the incumbent; four of the five failures hit the 16384-token cap. The mechanical root causes were all in rewriting the state: one rollout swapped a block other than the listed one and then reported the state unchanged under further applications (impossible), one traced indices to immediate fixed points and could not settle the swap target, and the one failure that terminated dropped every sub-step but the last, got a pure involution, and answered 2. The revision therefore forces untouched slots to be copied verbatim from the previous line, adds a fixed-point/duplicate audit on the composed operation, gives the nested-growing-blocks reason the composite cannot be independent order-2 swaps, and caps rechecking at one pass before committing.
